recommendation: Keep the source fix. It corrects the prior application location while preserving the work group decision not to add a birth address-use code; no further core or extension-pack work is indicated by the inspected evidence.
issue_request: FHIR-42765 asked for a birth value in the Address use/type value set because birthPlace uses Address. FHIR-I resolved the Applied issue as Not Persuasive with Modification: do not add a birth code, and add guidance to Address.use explaining that use is relevant for differentiating among multiple addresses and is typically omitted when an element or extension already implies the address purpose.
initial_application: Git commit b9dde86c67e28be13aec78419f01633b1501d2d0 appears to be the original FHIR-42765 application and introduced the approved guidance text into source/datatypes/address.xml. Current source inspection showed the guidance present but attached to the Address.type Comments cell, while Address.use retained only the older current/temporary/old comment.
additional_context: FHIR-I minutes for 2024-03-18 independently record the rationale, exact guidance, and 11-0-0 motion to accept. source/fhir.ini lists Address as an active datatype with the default datatypes page mapping, so source/datatypes/address.xml is in current build scope. The FHIR Extension Pack patient-birthPlace extension is Address-valued, supporting the decision that birth purpose is implicit in the extension and should not be duplicated as an Address.use code. Bounded Zulip searches found no directly relevant or conflicting discussion.
reconciliation: Moved the approved guidance into the Address.use Comments cell and removed it from the Address.type Comments cell, leaving Address.type focused on postal versus physical address semantics. The AddressUse code list remains home/work/temp/old/billing, with no birth code added.
source_changes: source/datatypes/address.xml: moved the approved Address.use omission guidance into the Address.use comment and removed it from the Address.type comment.
